scenes.problem: Do 2/3 and 6/9 name the same part of a whole?
rows: Split both same-sized wholes into 3 equal pieces.
Rewrite 2/3 as 2/3 and 6/9 as 2/3.
The numerators 2 and 2 match; the claim is yes.
scenes.memo: Do 2/3 and 6/9 name the same part of a whole? The common unit is 3; scaled counts are [2, 2]. Answer: yes.
scenes.misconception: Use equal-sized wholes and multiply numerator and denominator together; never compare only the bottom numbers.

rows: Split both same-sized wholes into 4 equal pieces.
Rewrite 3/4 as 3/4 and 6/8 as 3/4.
The numerators 3 and 3 match; the claim is yes.
scenes.memo: Are 3/4 and 6/8 equivalent? The common unit is 4; scaled counts are [3, 3]. Answer: yes.
scenes.misconception: Use equal-sized wholes and multiply numerator and denominator together; never compare only the bottom numbers.

scenes.problem: A learner claims 4/5 = 12/20. Test the claim.
rows: Split both same-sized wholes into 5 equal pieces.
Rewrite 4/5 as 4/5 and 12/20 as 3/5.
The numerators 4 and 3 differ; the claim is no.
scenes.memo: A learner claims 4/5 = 12/20. Test the claim. The common unit is 5; scaled counts are [4, 3]. Answer: no.
scenes.misconception: Use equal-sized wholes and multiply numerator and denominator together; never compare only the bottom numbers.

scenes.problem: Compare 1/2 and 2/3 using equal-sized fraction strips.
rows: Choose 6 equal parts for the two fraction strips.
Express 1/2 = 3/6 and 2/3 = 4/6.
Compare 3 and 4 equal parts: 1/2 < 2/3.
scenes.memo: Compare 1/2 and 2/3 using equal-sized fraction strips. The common unit is 6; scaled counts are [3, 4]. Answer: <.
scenes.misconception: Use equal-sized wholes and multiply numerator and denominator together; never compare only the bottom numbers.

scenes.problem: Arrange 1/2, 3/4 and 2/3 from least to greatest.
rows: Use strips divided into 12 equal parts.
The shaded counts in given order are 6, 9, 8 out of 12.
Order these counts from least to greatest: 1/2 < 2/3 < 3/4.
scenes.memo: Arrange 1/2, 3/4 and 2/3 from least to greatest. The common unit is 12; scaled counts are [6, 9, 8]. Answer: 1/2 < 2/3 < 3/4.

scenes.problem: Convert 1 3/4 into an improper fraction; show the whole and quarter pieces.
rows: Draw 1 complete unit strip and 3 of 4 equal pieces.
Count all 4-parts: 7 in total.
The equivalent improper fraction is 7/4.
scenes.memo: Convert 1 3/4 into an improper fraction; show the whole and quarter pieces. The common unit is 4; scaled counts are [7]. Answer: 7/4.

scenes.problem: Convert 17/6 into a mixed number and check by recombining sixths.

Count all 6-parts: 17 in total.
The equivalent mixed number is 2 5/6.
